rationale: Tests recall of paired directional terms applied in clinical sentences, which is the core skill established by this block on the language of anatomical location.
Tests understanding of the movement–plane–axis relationships that form the core concept of this block on body movements.
Tests recall of bone cells and the two-phase matrix that gives bone both hardness and toughness, the key concept established in this block on bone composition.
Tests recall of the specific bones that retain red marrow in the healthy adult, the clinically essential knowledge from this block that determines where marrow aspiration is performed.

Tests recall of the clinically essential dermatome landmarks that students must memorise for localising spinal cord lesions, assessing spinal block height, and interpreting the distribution of herpes zoster.
Tests recall of the five epidermal layers in their correct deep-to-superficial order, which determines how skin regenerates after injury — the key structural concept completed in this block.

Provides a visual explorer of the four main skin appendages just described, reinforcing that each is an epidermal downgrowth into the dermis — the fact that explains why partial-thickness burns heal and why graft donor sites close.
Tests recall of the key principles governing skin incision direction and scar quality, the central clinical application taught in this block on Langer's lines and skin creases.
